record.file_problem: The post is readable, but some math-rendered expressions and numeric values are missing or stripped in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The post presents toy-transformer results and an explicit refinement of the one-dimensional feature picture: it argues for sparse, multidimensional subspaces and reports activations matching a multidimensional belief geometry.
record.gate_note: The tested result is belief-state geometry in transformers trained on a synthetic two-component HMM mixture. The post does not test sparse-feature competition under the conditions of Toy Models of Superposition, SAE recovery or canonicality, or feature geometry in real LLMs. Cited results are not recorded as rows. The post's qualitative geometry descriptions are included; some additional numerical details are missing from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The post argues that the 'sparse one-dimensional features' picture needs restating as sparse multi-dimensional subspaces. It backs this with a toy-transformer result: a 5-D belief geometry linearly embedded in the residual stream that collapses onto one component's subspace as evidence accumulates. This bears on V6 only. There is no capacity pressure, no feature count above dimension and no SAE comparison, so it is a scope argument rather than a direct test of superposition.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also stress three points. The geometry is not forced by next-token prediction alone. It appears most cleanly with small initialization. Their picture is a refinement to, and consistent with, multi-dimensional linear representation work, not a refutation of SAEs.
record.recipe_differences: The study constructs a nonergodic mixture of two HMM components, trains a transformer on next-token prediction, and measures whether a linear map recovers belief geometry. It does not apply the original Toy Models of Superposition method or measure its feature geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The post reports that filtering to lower posterior entropy changes the apparent dimensionality and component-cone geometry. It also says the canonical low-dimensional representations emerge most cleanly with small initial weights.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear belief-state representation of a hierarchical, nonergodic generator, with telescoping cones scaled by the component posterior. Next-token training yields a representation that carries more than the next-token distribution.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transformers trained on mixtures of generators linearly represent per-component belief geometry, scaled by posterior component weight.

record.problems: Evidence is from a synthetic two-component task and a toy transformer, not real LLMs. The geometry and PCA descriptions are primarily qualitative, with no uncertainty estimates or numerical CEV values. Some numeric details, including a final-block R² value, are missing from the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: The appendix says the final transformer block reaches an R² value, but the number is missing in the supplied text, so it is not recorded as a result row.

untested.parts: No sparse-feature toy model with more features than dimensions; no sparsity-dependent phase transition; no nearly orthogonal or polytope geometry.
No neuron-level polysemanticity; no importance or capacity allocation.
No real LLMs; no SAE or dictionary recovery.
SAEs are discussed only as motivation; their completeness, stability and canonicality are not tested.
Real models are not examined. Nor is it tested whether 1-D dictionary features would fail on this geometry, or whether multi-dimensional subspaces are superposed beyond the available dimensions.

missing.what: Per-layer regression floors: R² tracks excess loss in every layer past the first, and the final-block R² value is stripped from the text.
Dependence on initialization: canonical low-dimensional geometry emerges most cleanly with small initial weights (rich regime). This is a method sensitivity relevant to V6 scope.
missing.locator: Did it have to be this way?

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' label overstates the result. The study has no capacity-pressure or superposition setting, and its linear-probe evidence is compatible with 1-D directions. The comments mention 'subspace superposition' as future work, which confirms that superposition itself is not tested here. This is a blog post and is not peer reviewed.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not test whether sparse features exceeding dimensionality are stored as overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, or a sparsity-dependent transition and regular geometry.
It does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise from limited capacity, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
It does not test polysemanticity arising for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The experiments use a transformer trained on synthetic data, not real LLMs; they do not test feature spread across neurons or recovery by a dictionary or SAE.
The post discusses sparse autoencoders and proposes a refinement to their motivating feature picture, but does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical.
The evidence concerns belief geometry in a synthetic-data transformer, not whether all features in real models are multidimensional or whether conventional superposition features are one-dimensional.

rows.check: Lowering posterior entropy makes the CEV curves climb faster and collapses the other component's cone. This shows sparsity at the level of whole multi-dimensional subspaces. No CEV numbers are given and the baseline is unspecified.

relationships.condition: 4-layer toy transformer trained on an equal-weight nonergodic mixture of two Mess3 HMMs
relationships.reason: The co-active units are multi-dimensional belief subspaces that switch on and off sparsely by component (r3, r4). So 1-D features are not the natural unit for nonergodic data. But superposition is never shown, and a 1-D decomposition is not ruled out (r1 cannot distinguish).
relationships.display_finding: The co-active units were multi-dimensional belief subspaces that switch on and off sparsely by mixture component, so 1-D features are not the natural unit for such data. Superposition was never shown, and a 1-D decomposition could not be ruled out.
